title: Intel Advances US Factory Expansion as Chip Demand Grows
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Intel is advancing factory projects in Arizona and Ohio, signaling greater confidence in future chip demand after years of delays and tighter spending controls.

The company says construction and equipment installation are underway at Fab 62, its next manufacturing facility at the Ocotillo campus in Arizona. Operations are expected to begin by the end of 2028. In New Albany, Ohio, crews have installed the first major structural truss at Intel’s planned factory, marking another step toward expanding American semiconductor production.

These developments matter because a factory building alone cannot manufacture chips. Installing sophisticated production equipment requires substantial additional investment, making that stage a stronger indication of commitment than construction milestones by themselves.

The expansion also reflects Intel’s broader domestic manufacturing network. Oregon anchors advanced research and process development, while Arizona combines manufacturing with packaging research, assembly and testing. New Mexico supports advanced packaging production.

Bloomberg reports that chief executive Lip-Bu Tan has made expansion dependent on sufficient customer demand. Continued investment therefore suggests management sees a stronger business case for additional capacity, although construction progress does not establish that every future production line has secured customers.

Intel is pursuing two related opportunities: meeting demand for its own processors and building a foundry business that manufactures chips for outside companies. Demand for processors used in data centers supporting artificial intelligence has increased, helping strengthen the rationale for new investment.

However, the turnaround remains unfinished. Intel must translate spending into reliable production, competitive technology and sustained customer orders. Its ambitions also face intense competition from established semiconductor manufacturers.

For now, the Arizona and Ohio updates offer tangible evidence that previously delayed projects are moving forward. Their ultimate significance will depend on whether Intel can bring facilities online efficiently and fill them with profitable work as demand develops over the next several years.

Sources:
Bloomberg: “Intel Touts Factory Expansion Progress in Sign of Growing Demand”, October 21, 2026.
The Edge Malaysia: Bloomberg report republished, October 22, 2026.
Intel: “Building America’s Capacity to Innovate” — the company’s primary update on Arizona and Ohio construction.
